List every run of adjacent digits of a given length in a string of digits, in order.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/series) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: series.nomi
//# The runs of adjacent digits of one length in a string of digits.

/// Why a series has no slices of the length asked for.
pub enum Error {
    EmptySeries
    ZeroLength
    NegativeLength
    LengthTooLarge
}

/// Every run of `length` adjacent characters in `series`, in the order they
/// start. Runs overlap, and equal runs are all kept.
pub fn slices(series: String, length: Int) -> Result<List<String>, Error> {
    size = String.length(series)

    if size == 0 {
        Err(.EmptySeries)
    } else if length < 0 {
        Err(.NegativeLength)
    } else if length == 0 {
        Err(.ZeroLength)
    } else if length > size {
        Err(.LengthTooLarge)
    } else {
        series
        |> Iter.windows(length)
        |> Iter.map(String.join)
        |> Iter.to_list()
        |> Ok()
    }
}

// FILE: series_test.nomi
import series.{self, Error}

test "slices" {
    cases = [
        #("slices of one from one", "1", 1, ["1"]),
        #("slices of one from two", "12", 1, ["1", "2"]),
        #("slices of two", "35", 2, ["35"]),
        #("slices of two overlap", "9142", 2, ["91", "14", "42"]),
        #("slices can include duplicates", "777777", 3, ["777", "777", "777", "777"]),
        #(
            "slices of a long series",
            "918493904243",
            5,
            ["91849", "18493", "84939", "49390", "93904", "39042", "90424", "04243"],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, digits, length, expected), description {
        assert series.slices(digits, length) == Ok(expected)
    }
}

test "errors" {
    cases = [
        #("slice length is too large", "12345", 6, Error.LengthTooLarge),
        #("slice length is way too large", "12345", 42, .LengthTooLarge),
        #("slice length cannot be zero", "12345", 0, .ZeroLength),
        #("slice length cannot be negative", "123", -1, .NegativeLength),
        #("empty series is invalid", "", 1, .EmptySeries),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, digits, length, expected), description {
        assert series.slices(digits, length) == Err(expected)
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Errors are an `Error` enum with one variant per canonical message. The checks run in the order the canonical cases need: an empty series is `EmptySeries` even when the length is also too large.
- The validation is an `if`/`else if` chain, since each condition compares different values; a `case` on `length` would need a guard on every arm.
- The runs are `Iter.windows(series, length)` over the string's graphemes, each joined back into a string. The function works on graphemes, not only digits.
- The test file splits the canonical cases into two `subtests` tables, one for `Ok` results and one for errors, so each table makes one claim. The test binds the input as `digits`, since `series` is the module's name there.
